Wuthering Waves is a fun gacha game with great combat and smooth movement. The world looks beautiful, and the characters are enjoyable. Graphics impressive af. The story starts slowly, and there can be small performance issues, but overall the game is very good and enjoyable to play.

9/10 – I recommend it.

As a launch day player, I can't recommend this game enough. The graphics are stunning, the combat is very fun and the exploration is pretty easy. The characters all have great designs and animations. The game is very generous with the rewards as well, though it feels like those are starting to dwindle with world exploration, but I'll mention it later.
I love how the devs are always working on making sure the game is optimized, especially for PCs like mine.

For the cons, I've noticed that the story tends to forget about previous characters and areas after we go to a new place or get a new patch. I understand that the updates want to revolve around the character(s) that are new in that update but they screw over the the rest of the cast by doing that. 
The story does have a few tropes that it follows, the main one being "New area, New Waifu". It doesn't bother me that much, I just wish it wasn't so forced. 
Now, for the exploration rewards. There haven't been nearly as many chests in the new areas (Lahai Roi-Mengzhou) compared to the previous ones (Jinzhou-Septimont)

For those who love to collect the male characters like me, expect to wait a good while in between them. Kuro likes to follow a "2 new men per year" theme with WuWa. At least that gives us plenty of time to save for them lol.
Laha-Roi saved the game imo, new combat is very fun, fixed graphics, stutters and other bugs. I give it a solid 7.8/10, needs a little more polishing but it's very promising

I played for about 59 hours, so this isn’t a knee-jerk negative review.
The game has real strengths: the combat feels good, the world is interesting, and at first it genuinely feels promising. Unfortunately, the longer you play, the more the progression systems completely undermine that experience.
The gacha is extremely predatory. Materials are painfully scarce, and your world level increases faster than your character power, so instead of feeling rewarded for playing, you feel punished for leveling up. Progress doesn’t feel earned—it feels restricted.
The breaking point for me was realizing that no matter how much I played—days, weeks—I simply couldn’t meaningfully pull characters. I liked a new character they introduced, kept playing consistently, and yet made zero real progress toward obtaining her. There was no sense of “I’m getting closer.” Just effort with no payoff.
What’s worse is that I didn’t even consciously quit. I just… stopped opening the game. The motivation disappeared naturally once it became clear that my time wasn’t being respected.
If you plan to spend money, you might have a different experience. If you’re hoping for fair progression through play alone, be aware that this game may quietly burn you out rather than hook you.
I’m leaving this review so others can decide with open eyes.

I avoid gatcha games like the plague but gave this one a crack as I heard good things. Initial experience is that it's pretty bland for the first 30hrs or so as you do the 1.0 content. This progressively gets better as you get into the patches and eventually becomes pretty engaging both narrative and gameplay wise.

As a new player you're constantly crushed by fomo and time gated mechanics which suck, but there is a lot of content for the F2P player so you feel like you can get some good value for time from it.

The gambling is done relatively well with very generous free coins, but don't bother spending on the slot machine the exchange rate is completely insane. Something towards £30 for 10 pulls which is just fleecing when the rare characters can take 100+ pulls if you're unlucky.

God have mercy if you don't get a good 5* from your free coins because you will have a giant crash out if you don't. This might be foreshadowing for me when they eventually rerun Carlotta...

I started with Genshin and played for years, but the burnout hit HARD after the game didn't change for so long. I looked for something new and waited for Wuthering Waves’ release. It was SO WORTH IT! It was (and still is) the breath of fresh air I needed. Sure, the release was a bit bumpy, I guess, but the developers worked hard to fix everything. The game looks awesome, you even have some setting to make it even prettier too. 
I feel like my time is appreciated in wuwa. No more losing a 50/50 on a weapon banner since it's guaranteed, leveling characters is quicker, exploring the map is much easier with a proper lootmapper, and it’s also so much more fun! Fighting looks amazing, dodging is rewarding, and you can skip quests if they bore you (but trust me, the quests are actually pretty well made, especially main quest of course), events are fun and more rewarding, characters are really pretty and have lots of cool animations. Basically, the game hit the sweet spot for me. I 100% recommend it. ♥
